ic.utility_name: Virginia Electric & Power Co (Dominion Energy Virginia)
ic.rule_summary: Dominion's residential/small-C&I tariff sub-caps nonresidential systems at 1 MW (below the 3 MW statewide statutory ceiling). Following the SCC's April 30, 2026 final order (Case No. PUR-2025-00079), Dominion is rolling out a 'NEM 2.0' tariff for customers who interconnect after the order's effective date: 1:1 kWh crediting and 12-month (annual) netting are preserved, but the year-end net-excess-generation cash-out rate rises to $0.05829/kWh (includes a new $0.01/kWh credit for avoided RPS/REC compliance cost) and a $1/month administrative fee applies. The SCC rejected Dominion's proposed $100-750 application fee and its proposed 30-minute netting/dollar-based interval crediting. Pre-order NEM 1.0 customers remain grandfathered indefinitely and may switch to NEM 2.0 only if it becomes more favorable to them. Low-income customers may choose whichever tariff (legacy or NEM 2.0) is more favorable. Separately, the SCC-authorized standby charge threshold rises from 15 kW AC to 20 kW AC effective 7/1/2026 under HB 1255.

market.struct: $/MW-day UCAP capacity payment cleared in Base Residual Auction; single year-round CP product
market.val: Set by BRA clearing price (see BRA rows); bounded by FERC-approved Market Seller Offer Cap tied to Net ACR
market.limits: Must perform during all Performance Assessment Hours across the Delivery Year; 24x365 obligation; no seasonal or hourly call cap

market.struct: $/MWh payment for reserve capacity deliverable within 30 minutes
market.val: Not independently confirmed for 2026; published via PJM Data Miner 2 Day-Ahead Ancillary Service LMPs feed
market.limits: 30-minute response requirement

market.struct: $/MWh capacity payment cleared in the 10-minute co-optimized reserve market; Tier 1 is spare energy from online resources deliverable within 10 minutes while Tier 2 is called only when Tier 1 is insufficient
market.val: Clearing prices vary by hour and reserve zone and were not independently confirmed for 2026; PJM added a 30% adder to the Synchronized Reserve requirement in May 2023 after under-performance during reserve events
market.limits: Must respond within 10 minutes and sustain for the event duration; deployed via a PJM-declared Synchronized Reserve Event

MN.rule_citation: Minn. Stat. 216B.164; Minn. Rules ch. 7835 (7835.4013-4015); MN Distributed Interconnection Process (MN DIP) and Technical Interconnection and Interoperability Requirements (TIIR), Docket E999/CI-16-521
MN.applies_to: All utilities (IOU + co-op + muni; compensation mechanics differ by ownership type)
MN.nem_successor: No mandatory statewide successor for rooftop NEM; Xcel Value of Solar (VOS) tariff is optional alternative for Xcel residential/small customers and became mandatory for new Xcel community solar garden (CSG) subscribers under a phased ARR-to-VOS transition effective April 1 2025 (Docket E002/M-21-694)
MN.nem_sizing_rule: <=120% of prior 12-month (or projected) on-site consumption combined with any community solar garden subscription (Minn. Stat. 216B.164 Subd.4c; 216B.1641)
MN.export_credit_basis: 1:1 retail (Average Retail Utility Energy Rate, systems <40 kW AC); avoided-cost/simultaneous purchase-and-sale rate or time-of-day rate for 40kW-1MW; value-of-DER stack (VOS) optional for Xcel, mandatory for new Xcel CSG subscribers
MN.export_credit_value: Average Retail Utility Energy Rate set annually per utility, varies by utility (statewide average roughly $0.12-0.14/kWh); Xcel VOS approx. $0.1909/kWh for CSG subscribers as filed 2025, stepping down for C&I subscribers (~$0.13/kWh 2025, ~$0.12/kWh 2026)
MN.credit_rollover: Monthly netting under 40kW; annual banking option for 40kW-1MW systems
MN.annual_true_up: Excess annual banked credits for public-utility customers cashed out at avoided cost; co-op/muni excess credits canceled with no payment (Minn. Stat. 216B.164 Subd.3a and Subd.3(f))
MN.ic_standard: IEEE 1547-2018 + UL 1741-SA/SB (Minnesota was first state to adopt IEEE 1547-2018 statewide via TIIR, Commission order Jan 22 2020; docket E999/CI-16-521 remains open for Phase II refinements)
MN.ic_application_fee: Simplified process: $100 + $1/kWac; Study process: $1000 + $2/kWac; statewide $30 surcharge added to all applications
MN.external_disconnect: Utility discretion (typically required for larger/study-track systems; often waived for UL1741-SB inverter-based systems under simplified process — confirm per utility)
MN.insurance_required: Not specified in statewide rule; utility-specific in interconnection agreement
MN.ic_timeline_days: ic_timeline_days not specified as single statewide statutory number in sources reviewed; MN DIP sets tiered review deadlines by track (see MN DIP document)
MN.non_export_option: Yes — defined non-export operating mode exists (MN DIP Exhibit B for Energy Storage; Xcel Energy MN Electric Energy Storage Interconnection Guidelines) using control-system settings and bi-directional metering to enforce zero export
MN.storage_counts_toward_cap: Yes (storage nameplate/inverter capacity at point of interconnection generally counts toward system size for NEM/DIP purposes; confirm per utility tariff)
MN.standby_charge: Not specified in statewide statute; co-op/muni may impose DG fixed-cost recovery fee (Minn. Stat. 216B.164 Subd.3(a)); public utilities barred from DG-specific fixed fees beyond standard retail fixed charges

WI.rule_citation: Wis. Admin. Code PSC 119 (interconnection); no statewide net metering statute — parallel generation buyback rates set utility-by-utility via individual tariff dockets
WI.applies_to: IOU + co-op + muni (PSC 119 interconnection technical rules apply to all DG facilities <=15 MW seeking interconnection to a utility distribution system; buyback/compensation tariffs are NOT statewide and are set per-utility)
WI.nem_successor: No formal statewide NEM successor; each utility runs its own parallel-generation buyback tariff. PSC reopened a statewide Net Energy Metering investigation (2023-2025) and commissioned a Value of Solar Study (VOSS) literature review with Berkeley Lab/national labs; as of the Sept 2024 open meeting the Commission had taken no policy action and was awaiting the VOSS literature review — docket remains open and outcome could reset buyback rates statewide within the next 1-2 years
WI.nem_aggregate_cap: No statewide aggregate cap (varies by utility tariff)
WI.nem_sizing_rule: Not standardized statewide; individual utility tariffs may impose sizing limits tied to historical usage
WI.export_credit_basis: Buy-all-sell-all / avoided-cost buyback rate for excess above NEM threshold, set per-utility tariff (not 1:1 retail beyond the NEM threshold in most IOU territories)
WI.export_credit_value: Varies sharply by utility — e.g. We Energies buyback ~$0.0317/kWh (2026); WPS/WPL retail-rate net metering up to 20 kW; see FILE 2 utility rows for utility-specific figures
WI.ic_standard: IEEE 1547-2018 + IEEE 1547.1-2020 incorporated by reference into PSC 119 (effective per PSC 119 rule revision)
WI.ic_application_fee: Not standardized statewide; varies by utility
WI.ic_study_trigger_kw: Not standardized statewide; varies by utility (larger/complex projects trigger supplemental review under PSC 119)
WI.ic_timeline_days: Not specified as single statewide statutory number; PSC 119 sets tiered review timelines by DG category
WI.grid_charging_allowed: Unclear (varies by utility; grid-charging treatment is not addressed uniformly in PSC 119 and is a live issue in the NEM/VOSS docket)
WI.non_export_option: Yes — PSC 119 defines a non-exporting Category 1 pathway for co-located storage no larger than 20 kW paired with a non-exporting DG resource no larger than 20 kW, which qualifies for simplified/expedited review
WI.storage_counts_toward_cap: Yes for exporting configurations (storage nameplate counts toward DG facility capacity category under PSC 119); non-exporting storage handled separately under Category 1
WI.standby_charge: Not specified in statewide rule; some utilities (e.g. We Energies) assess a Generation Customer Charge (~$0.059/day) on DG customers — utility-specific

IA.jurisdiction_body: Iowa Utilities Commission (formerly Iowa Utilities Board)
IA.rule_citation: Iowa Code 476.49 (SF 583, enacted 2020); 199 IAC Chapter 45 (interconnection technical standards)
IA.applies_to: IOU only for the codified SF 583 inflow-outflow regime (applies to rate-regulated utilities i.e. MidAmerican and Alliant/Interstate Power and Light); municipal utilities and rural electric cooperatives are exempt from IUC rate/NEM jurisdiction and set their own net metering/DG policies
IA.nem_successor: SF 583 (2020) replaced true net metering with an inflow/outflow billing structure for new DG customers starting July 1 2020; MidAmerican tariff effective Nov 24 2020, Alliant/IPL tariff effective Dec 30 2020. Outflow rate initially set equal to the retail (inflow) rate but is scheduled to transition toward a value-of-solar-informed rate once the 5% statewide penetration trigger is reached or by 2027, whichever first — a Value of Solar study/proceeding is the anticipated successor mechanism and is not yet finalized as of last verification
IA.nem_aggregate_cap: 5% of each utility's statewide peak electric demand (statutory trigger for VOS proceeding; current subscription level not confirmed in sources reviewed)
IA.export_credit_basis: 1:1 retail equivalent under inflow-outflow (outflow credited at same rate as inflow/retail rate, i.e. functionally 1:1 at present)
IA.export_credit_value: Outflow rate = retail rate as of 2020 tariffs (MidAmerican eff. 11/24/2020; Alliant/IPL eff. 12/30/2020); scheduled to move toward value-of-solar basis post-trigger — confirm current cents/kWh in utility tariff
IA.credit_rollover: Monthly billing under inflow-outflow (kWh-for-kWh at time of use within billing period; no long-term banking under strict inflow-outflow design — confirm)
IA.annual_true_up: Monthly per SF 583 inflow-outflow structure; no annual true-up mechanism identified in sources reviewed
IA.ic_standard: IEEE 1547-2018 (incorporated into 199 IAC 45.3, effective per rule dated April 6 2018 edition; rule revision effective 7/16/2025 per Iowa Admin Code updates)
IA.ic_fast_track_kw: NEM/interconnection uses tiered Levels 1-4 application process (Level 1 = smallest/fastest per 199 IAC 45); exact kW threshold for Level 1 not confirmed in sources reviewed
IA.ic_simplified_kw: Not confirmed in sources reviewed for Level 2/3 thresholds
IA.ic_study_trigger_kw: Not confirmed in sources reviewed (Level 3/4 studies triggered for larger/more complex systems per 199 IAC 45)
IA.ic_timeline_days: Not confirmed in sources reviewed (tiered by Level under 199 IAC 45)
IA.non_export_option: Unclear — non-export pathway not confirmed in sources reviewed for 199 IAC Chapter 45; recommend direct rule review
IA.storage_counts_toward_cap: Unclear — not confirmed whether storage nameplate counts toward the 1 MW AC / 110%-of-usage sizing cap

ND.rule_citation: N.D. Admin. Code (net metering rule adopted 1991); no statewide interconnection procedures rule (confirmed by Freeing the Grid / IREC-Vote Solar 2026 scorecard: ND has not adopted statewide interconnection procedures)
ND.applies_to: IOU only (net metering rule applies only to investor-owned utility customers; municipal utilities and rural electric cooperatives are NOT covered and set their own policies at their discretion)
ND.nem_successor: No formal statewide interconnection procedure exists; net-excess-generation purchase rule dates to 1991 and is thin — avoided-cost buyback only, not retail net metering. No successor tariff or active docket identified in sources reviewed
ND.export_credit_value: Not specified statewide; avoided cost is utility-specific and not published centrally
ND.credit_rollover: Monthly (net excess generation settled monthly at avoided cost per source reviewed)
ND.ic_standard: Not specified — no statewide interconnection technical standard identified; utilities individually reference IEEE 1547 in their own tariffs
ND.non_export_option: No statewide rule — utility discretion; no defined statewide non-export pathway identified

SD.rule_citation: S.D. Codified Laws 49-34A (utility service territory law); no statewide net metering statute or rule — PUC regulates small generator interconnection practice and mandates utilities purchase excess generation at avoided cost, but has explicitly declined to adopt net metering
SD.applies_to: IOU only for PUC-regulated interconnection/purchase obligation (municipal utilities and rural electric cooperatives largely outside PUC rate jurisdiction and set their own terms)
SD.nem_successor: No statewide rule — no successor because there was never a net metering program to succeed. PUC has published an explicit rationale (Compensation FAQ page) for why net metering has not been adopted; avoided-cost purchase obligation is the sole statewide mechanism, confirmed current as of Oct 10 2024 PUC Solar Energy FAQ
SD.export_credit_value: Avoided-cost rates are utility-specific and filed with/approved by the PUC for IOUs (publicly viewable at puc.sd.gov/energy/rrrates.aspx); no single statewide cents/kWh figure
SD.credit_rollover: Not specified — no banking/rollover mechanism under avoided-cost purchase
SD.ic_standard: Not specified — no statewide interconnection technical standard identified in sources reviewed; utilities individually reference IEEE 1547 in their own interconnection agreements
SD.non_export_option: No statewide rule — utility discretion; no defined statewide non-export pathway identified

MI.rule_citation: MCL 460.1173; PA 341/342 of 2016; PA 235 of 2023; Mich. Admin. Code R 460.901a-1026 (MIXDG rules, eff. 4/25/2023)
MI.applies_to: IOU + AES (member co-ops exempt but many voluntarily participate)
MI.nem_successor: Distributed Generation (DG) program under PA 341/342 replaced net metering for all new customers starting 2016-2019 (utility-specific transition dates); billed via separate inflow/outflow metering rather than net kWh. Legacy NEM customers grandfathered for 10 years from enrollment date, with storage additions permitted without loss of grandfathering per R 460.920(5)(m) if not a 'material modification'.
MI.nem_aggregate_cap: 10% of utility's average in-state peak load over preceding 5 years (raised from 1% by PA 235 of 2023, eff. 2023); allocated not less than 5% for <=20kW projects and not more than 5% for >20-550kW projects
MI.nem_sizing_rule: <=110% of customer's average annual electricity consumption (raised from 100% by PA 235)
MI.export_credit_basis: unbundled generation rate (LMP-based for DTE; utility-specific avoided-cost/power-supply component for others)
MI.export_credit_value: DTE Electric: outflow credited at monthly average real-time LMP at DTE load nodes, power-supply/PSCR component only, not delivery; Consumers Energy and other utility rates vary by tariff rider - see utility file
MI.credit_rollover: monthly netting of inflow/outflow (not indefinite rollover)
MI.annual_true_up: Excess outflow credited monthly at outflow rate; no annual banking of kWh as under retail NEM since inflow and outflow are billed as separate line items each month
MI.ic_standard: IEEE 1547-2018 + UL 1741-SB (MIXDG rules eff. 4/25/2023; supersedes prior IEEE 1547-2003/UL1741-SA under rescinded net metering rules)
MI.ic_application_fee: $300 pre-application report cap; fast track initial review $100+$1/kWac (certified) or $100+$2/kWac (non-certified); fast track supplemental review cap $1000; non-export track $100+$1-2/kWac; legacy NEM/DG program app fee combined with fast-track fees capped at $50 total (R 460.926)
MI.external_disconnect: Utility discretion (not explicitly mandated statewide in MIXDG rules; determined by utility interconnection procedures per R 460.920)
MI.insurance_required: Not specified in state rule; utility-specific
MI.ic_timeline_days: Level 1/2/3 use statewide standard agreement; commission order deadlines are 360 days for utility to file procedures, per-application timelines set in utility-approved procedures (R 460.920)
MI.non_export_option: Yes - explicit rule-based non-export/limited-export path via R 460.980: reverse power relay (0.1% export default), under-power relay, small-DER-vs-load exemption (<=50% of min host load), reduced output setting, or NRTL-certified power control system with 2-second trip on inadvertent export >30s
MI.storage_counts_toward_cap: Unclear - not explicitly addressed in DG program rules reviewed; battery kW is not separately capped from PV kW under the 550kW system cap
MI.standby_charge: Not identified in rules reviewed for residential/small C&I; utilities may petition for utility-specific standby/facility charges via general rate case

IN.applies_to: IOU only (municipal and REMC/cooperative utilities largely exempt and set own rules)
IN.nem_successor: SEA 309 (2017, IC 8-1-40) closed 1:1 retail-rate net metering to new customers effective for IOU customers who did not enroll by a utility-specific 2017-2022 cutoff (approx. mid-2022 for most IOUs, per 30-month transition after 2018 enactment cutoff). Successor is the Excess Distributed Generation (EDG) tariff: excess (outflow) energy credited at 125% of the utility's prior-calendar-year average marginal/wholesale price of energy (IC 8-1-40-17), typically ~3-5 cents/kWh vs 14-17 cents/kWh retail. Grandfathering: systems installed/enrolled before 2018 retain full 1:1 net metering until July 1, 2047; systems enrolled between 2018 and the utility's net-metering closure date (the '2022 cohort') retain full net metering until July 1, 2032. After the respective sunset date, grandfathered customers move to the EDG rate.
IN.nem_aggregate_cap: Not specified as a statewide numeric aggregate cap under SEA 309 (unlike MI's 10% cap structure) - EDG is open-ended/uncapped by kW as a matter of state law; utility-specific queue/study limits may apply
IN.nem_sizing_rule: Generator nameplate capacity limited to the lesser of 1 MW or customer's average annual electricity consumption at the premises
IN.export_credit_value: 125% of the utility's average marginal/wholesale energy price for the prior calendar year (IC 8-1-40-17); e.g. AES Indiana 3.9350 cents/kWh effective 7/1/2024, updated annually via March 1 compliance filing - see utility file for other IOUs
IN.credit_rollover: indefinite (EDG credit balance carries forward indefinitely while customer remains on the rider; forfeited to FAC upon account closure)
IN.annual_true_up: No fixed annual true-up date under EDG; credit accumulates indefinitely as a running balance offsetting future bills down to the minimum charge
IN.ic_standard: IEEE 1547 (referenced generally; UL 1741 as certification basis - 2018 edition transition referenced in pending 170 IAC 4-4.3 rule revisions not yet confirmed finalized)
IN.ic_application_fee: Not specified as a statewide fixed fee schedule in rule text reviewed - utility-specific
IN.ic_study_trigger_kw: Above Level 1 threshold (>10kW triggers Level 2/3 review)
IN.external_disconnect: Utility discretion (not a blanket statewide requirement identified in 170 IAC 4-4.3 sections reviewed)
IN.insurance_required: Liability insurance required per 170 IAC 4-4.3-10 for customer-owned generator equipment, maintained continuously while interconnected
IN.ic_timeline_days: Level 1: 10 business days to confirm completeness + 15 business days to approve/deny (statutory deadlines in 170 IAC 4-4.3-6); Level 2/3 timelines longer and utility-procedure-specific
IN.non_export_option: Not addressed as a defined statewide non-export path in 170 IAC 4-4.3 sections reviewed; utility-specific treatment likely required for storage-paired systems - see gaps file
IN.storage_counts_toward_cap: Unclear - EDG eligibility is based on generator nameplate capacity vs. average annual consumption; whether battery kW is included in 'generator nameplate capacity' not confirmed in statute text reviewed
IN.standby_charge: Not identified in rule/statute text reviewed

OH.applies_to: IOU only (municipal and cooperative/REMC utilities exempt from PUCO net metering and interconnection rules; set own policies)
OH.nem_successor: Ohio never adopted a EDG/DG-successor program like MI or IN - net metering remains the statewide framework, but excess generation is credited only at the energy-only ('unbundled generation') component of the utility's Standard Service Offer (SSO) rather than the full bundled retail rate, which includes T&D, capacity, and riders. This produces retail-NEM-like mechanics (single bidirectional meter, monthly netting) but avoided-cost-like economics, since the SSO energy component excludes delivery charges.
OH.nem_aggregate_cap: Not specified as a numeric statewide aggregate cap in OAC 4901:1-10-28 (no MI/IN-style program-wide kW or % cap identified)
OH.nem_sizing_rule: <=120% of customer-generator's average annual electricity requirement (based on prior 3 years of utility-supplied electricity where available)
OH.export_credit_value: Energy-only component of the electric utility's Standard Service Offer (SSO); exact cents/kWh varies by utility and SSO auction cycle - see utility file for current per-utility SSO generation rates
OH.credit_rollover: indefinite (continuously carries forward as a monetary credit on future bills; utility is not required to cash out - credit may be lost if customer stops taking service or doesn't use it)
OH.annual_true_up: No mandatory annual cash-out/true-up identified in rule text - credit carries forward indefinitely rather than being zeroed out annually
OH.ic_standard: IEEE 1547 (per OAC 4901:1-22-03 Technical Interconnection and Interoperability Requirements, TIIR) + UL 1741
OH.ic_application_fee: $300 non-refundable pre-application report fee (optional, 14-day turnaround); Level 1 application fee capped at $50 and may be waived
OH.ic_study_trigger_kw: 25 (above Level 1 export capacity threshold of 25kW; Level 2 covers roughly 10kW-2MW per secondary sources, Level 3 detailed study for larger/complex projects)
OH.external_disconnect: Utility discretion (not identified as a blanket statewide mandate in rule text reviewed for Level 1)
OH.insurance_required: Not identified as a statewide net-metering/interconnection requirement in rule text reviewed
OH.ic_timeline_days: Level 1: EDU must confirm completeness within 14 calendar days, then complete review and notify applicant within 21 calendar days (30 days for hybrid facilities) of complete application; interconnection agreement issued within 10 days of approval. Level 2/3: EDU has 21 calendar days to confirm application completeness; longer study timelines apply.
OH.non_export_option: Hybrid/DER facilities (which include storage) are explicitly recognized in Level 1 review with a longer 30-day (vs 21-day) review timeframe, indicating storage-paired systems are accommodated but not fast-tracked identically to PV-only; a defined relay/control-based non-export interconnection path was not confirmed in the sections of OAC 4901:1-22 reviewed - see gaps file
OH.storage_counts_toward_cap: Unclear - the 120% sizing rule is based on customer electricity requirements, not generator/storage nameplate; whether battery kW counts toward the 120% figure not confirmed in rule text reviewed
OH.standby_charge: Not identified in rule text reviewed

KY.rule_citation: SB 100 (2019), eff. 1/1/2020; KRS 278.465-278.467; PSC Administrative Case No. 2019-00256 (methodology); Interconnection and Net Metering Guidelines (PSC Order, Admin. Case 2008-00169, as updated)
KY.applies_to: IOU only (municipal utilities and rural electric cooperatives largely self-regulated/exempt from PSC net metering rate-setting, though many voluntarily follow similar interconnection practices)
KY.nem_successor: SB 100 (2019) ended 1:1 retail-rate net metering for new customers effective 1/1/2020, replacing it with utility-specific PSC-approved compensation rates (each utility files its own 'NMS-2' or 'NM II' tariff based on an avoided-cost methodology - avoided energy, ancillary services, generation capacity, transmission capacity, distribution capacity, carbon/environmental compliance costs, and a jobs-benefit adder). SB 100 also raised the eligible system size cap from 30kW to 45kW. Customers already net metering (or grandfathered legacy tariff, 'NMS-1'/'NM I') as of the utility's transition date retain full 1:1 retail-rate net metering for 25 years from their enrollment date.
KY.nem_aggregate_cap: Not specified as a statewide numeric aggregate cap - SB 100 did not impose a program-wide MW/% cap; compensation rate (not enrollment volume) is the primary constraint
KY.nem_sizing_rule: Not specified as a uniform statewide % in statute reviewed - sizing generally tied to customer's own load (utility-specific)
KY.export_credit_value: Utility-specific PSC-approved 'NMS-2'/'NM II' rate, e.g. LG&E 6.924 cents/kWh and KU 7.366 cents/kWh (eff. for systems in service on/after 9/25/2021); Duke Energy Kentucky NM II 6.2924 cents/kWh residential / 6.3255 cents/kWh non-residential (eff. 1/1/2025) - see utility file for full detail
KY.credit_rollover: Not specified as indefinite/monthly/annual expiry in a single uniform statewide rule - varies by utility-specific NMS-2 tariff
KY.annual_true_up: Not specified uniformly - utility-specific tariff term
KY.ic_standard: IEEE 1547 (latest revision) + IEEE 1547.1 + UL 1741, per PSC Interconnection and Net Metering Guidelines
KY.ic_application_fee: Not specified as a statewide fixed fee schedule in guidelines reviewed - utility-specific
KY.external_disconnect: Not identified as a blanket statewide requirement in guidelines reviewed - utility discretion
KY.insurance_required: Not identified as a blanket statewide requirement in guidelines reviewed
KY.ic_timeline_days: Not specified as fixed statutory days in sources reviewed - governed by PSC Interconnection and Net Metering Guidelines and utility-specific procedures
KY.non_export_option: Not identified as a defined statewide non-export/limited-export interconnection path in guidelines reviewed - see gaps file
KY.storage_counts_toward_cap: Unclear - not confirmed whether battery kW counts toward the 45kW SB 100 system-size cap

IL.rule_citation: 83 Ill. Adm. Code 466 (interconnection); 83 Ill. Adm. Code 465 (net metering); 220 ILCS 5/16-107.5 as amended by CEJA (PA 102-0662)
IL.applies_to: IOU only (municipal utilities and electric cooperatives are exempt from ICC net metering/interconnection rules and set their own -- see CWLP delta row)
IL.nem_successor: Supply-only net metering ("Rider NM"): excess generation credited at the electricity supply/generation rate only, delivery/transmission charges excluded, effective for systems completing interconnection documentation on/after 1/1/2025 per CEJA. Systems fully installed, inspected, and interconnected with all paperwork received by the utility by 5:00pm CPT 12/31/2024 are grandfathered onto full-retail NEM for the life of the system (forfeited permanently if customer later accepts the DG/Smart Inverter Rebate).
IL.nem_aggregate_cap: 5% of the utility's prior-calendar-year peak demand (raised from 1% by CEJA); ComEd territory reported near/at cap in some feeder areas as of 2024-2025 dockets -- check current Illinois Shines/ICC capacity dashboards for live subscription level, not independently confirmed here
IL.nem_sizing_rule: Not independently verified in a hard sizing cap beyond the 2,000 kW (2 MW AC) eligibility ceiling in 220 ILCS 5/16-107.5
IL.export_credit_basis: 1:1 retail (legacy, grandfathered only); supply-rate-only net billing (new, post-1/1/2025)
IL.export_credit_value: Legacy 1:1 retail rate varies by utility rate class; new net billing credited at ComEd/Ameren electricity supply charge (cents/kWh), which floats with PJM/MISO wholesale costs -- no single statewide value published
IL.credit_rollover: Monthly netting with indefinite rollover of kWh credits under Rider NM; cash-out treatment for retail supplier switches not fully verified
IL.annual_true_up: Annual true-up practice varies by utility tariff (Rider NM); not fully verified from primary source for this pass
IL.ic_standard: IEEE 1547 (rule text cites IEEE 1547; ICC dockets and IREC's adoption tracker indicate a transition toward IEEE 1547-2018 / UL 1741-SB requirements -- exact effective date of mandatory 2018/SA-to-SB cutover not independently confirmed in this pass; flag as mid-transition)
IL.ic_application_fee: $50 (Level 1, lab-certified inverter-based facility <=25kW per EDC Level 1 application form); Level 2-4 fees not independently confirmed
IL.ic_study_trigger_kw: Screens/study thresholds begin above Level 1 (25kW); Level 3/4 full study triggers not independently confirmed with a specific kW number in this pass
IL.external_disconnect: Waived for Level 1 lab-certified inverter-based facilities per standard application form; requirement for larger Levels not independently confirmed
IL.insurance_required: General liability (e.g., homeowner's) insurance required; EDC named as additional insured where possible, per Level 1 standard agreement terms
IL.ic_timeline_days: Not independently confirmed (statutory timeline exists in 83 Ill. Adm. Code 466 but exact day-counts by level not verified this pass)
IL.non_export_option: Yes -- Level 1-4 application forms include explicit Limited Export and Non-Export control fields (reverse power protection, minimum power protection, directional power protection, or export-capacity-value relay control)
IL.storage_counts_toward_cap: Not independently confirmed whether battery kW/kWh counts toward the 2,000 kW system cap or the 5% aggregate cap

MO.rule_citation: RSMo 386.890 (Net Metering and Easy Connection Act); 20 CSR 4240-20.065 (Net Metering); 20 CSR 4240-20.060 (avoided-cost/cogeneration purchase rate)
MO.applies_to: IOU only (rural electric cooperatives and municipal utilities are exempt from MoPSC jurisdiction and net metering mandates; some voluntarily offer similar programs -- see City Utilities of Springfield/Columbia Water and Light/Independence P&L delta rows)
MO.nem_successor: No statutory phase-out identified; program continues under RSMo 386.890 subject to the statewide 5% aggregate cap. Monitor MoPSC dockets -- no active transition docket independently confirmed in this pass.
MO.nem_aggregate_cap: 5% of the electric utility's prior-year single-hour peak load (statewide cap per RSMo 386.890); current subscription level not independently confirmed for Ameren Missouri or Evergy Missouri West in this pass
MO.nem_sizing_rule: No explicit sizing-vs-consumption limit found in rule text beyond the 100 kW capacity ceiling; system intended primarily to offset the customer-generator's own load per definition in 20 CSR 4240-20.065(1)(C)5
MO.export_credit_basis: 1:1 retail during the billing period; monthly excess rolls forward at the utility's Commission-approved net metering rate (set equal to the utility's cogeneration/avoided-cost rate per 20 CSR 4240-20.065(6))
MO.export_credit_value: Net metering rate = utility's cogeneration (avoided-cost) rate, refiled biennially (odd years, by Jan 15) with the MoPSC; reported ~$0.03-0.04/kWh range for Ameren Missouri avoided cost vs ~$0.115-0.13/kWh retail -- not independently verified against a current tariff sheet in this pass
MO.annual_true_up: Any unused credit expires without compensation 12 months after issuance, or upon disconnection/termination of the net metering relationship, per 20 CSR 4240-20.065(5)(D)(6)(d)
MO.ic_standard: IEEE 1547a-2014 + UL 1703-2002 + UL 1741-2010 (as named explicitly in rule text; no confirmed transition to IEEE 1547-2018/UL 1741-SB identified in this pass -- flag as potentially outdated relative to national practice)
MO.ic_application_fee: No statewide application fee schedule found; utilities may charge for required metering/distribution upgrades reimbursed by the customer-generator
MO.ic_study_trigger_kw: Not explicitly tiered by kW in the rule; utility inspection/approval required for all systems with distinct timelines by size (see ic_timeline_days)
MO.external_disconnect: Utility may require a manual disconnect switch/breaker/fuse "in immediate proximity to metering equipment" at utility discretion -- not a blanket requirement for all systems
MO.insurance_required: Not required <=10 kW; required >10 kW at $100,000 minimum liability coverage per 20 CSR 4240-20.065(4)
MO.ic_timeline_days: 30 days for systems <=10 kW; 90 days for systems >10 kW (approval/denial notice timelines per rule's standard interconnection application)
MO.non_export_option: Not addressed in 20 CSR 4240-20.065 -- rule predates widespread storage deployment and contains no non-export/limited-export provisions; treat as a gap requiring case-by-case utility tariff review

AR.rule_citation: Ark. Code Ann. 23-18-601 et seq. (Arkansas Renewable Energy Development Act, as amended by Act 464 of 2019 and Act 278 of 2023); APSC Net-Metering Rules, Docket 23-021-R
AR.applies_to: IOU + co-op (statutory net metering applies broadly; electric cooperatives calculate avoided cost off Arkansas Electric Cooperative Corporation wholesale power costs rather than LMP -- see Ozarks Electric Cooperative delta row)
AR.nem_successor: Two-tier structure created by Act 278 of 2023: customers who submitted a Standard Interconnection Agreement before 12/31/2022 (and systems commissioned/interconnected before the 9/30/2024 cutoff referenced in program guidance) are "Legacy"/"Legacy-Transitional" customers grandfathered onto the pre-2023 1:1 rate structure for 20 years, through June 1, 2040 (Rule 2.06.A.1; Ark. Code Ann. 23-18-604(c)(11)(A)). Customers interconnecting after the cutoff take service under the utility's "Non-Legacy Net-Metering" tariff, compensated at Avoided Cost tied to the 12-month trailing average Locational Marginal Price (LMP) in the utility's MISO or SPP load zone (Rule 2.08); cooperatives base Avoided Cost on wholesale power purchased from Arkansas Electric Cooperative Corporation instead of LMP.
AR.nem_aggregate_cap: No statewide/aggregate percentage-of-peak-load cap in the rules; the binding constraint is the per-facility 1,000 kW administrative threshold (facilities above 1,000 kW up to 20 MW require Commission approval under Rule 2.06.B / Ark. Code Ann. 23-18-604(b)(9))
AR.nem_sizing_rule: Facility size limited to the lesser of (a) statutory nameplate generating capacity limit or (b) an estimate of output needed to meet the customer's "highest monthly usage" in the corresponding month (Rule 1.04(D))
AR.export_credit_basis: avoided cost (LMP-based for IOUs; cooperative wholesale-cost-based for co-ops) for Non-Legacy customers; 1:1 retail for grandfathered Legacy customers
AR.export_credit_value: Non-Legacy: avoided cost = 12-month trailing average hourly real-time LMP for the utility's MISO/SPP load zone, updated annually (Rule 2.08); no single statewide cents/kWh value published since it is utility- and zone-specific. Legacy: full retail rate (varies by rate class).
AR.credit_rollover: Not fully specified for Non-Legacy in the rules excerpted; Legacy 1:1 credits function as indefinite rollover through the 2040 grandfathering window
AR.annual_true_up: Not independently confirmed in this pass
AR.ic_standard: IEEE 1547 / UL 1741 referenced only generically ("...standards established by...IEEE...UL..."); no specific 1547-2018/UL1741-SB version cited in the rule text reviewed
AR.ic_fast_track_kw: Not independently confirmed with a specific fast-track kW threshold
AR.ic_simplified_kw: Not independently confirmed with a specific simplified-review kW threshold
AR.ic_application_fee: Not fixed in the rules -- utilities may charge a Commission-approved "standard one-time fee" to recover administrative/interconnection review costs; exact dollar amount is utility-specific tariff language, not stated generically in the rules
AR.external_disconnect: Waived for inverter-based systems if: (1) inverter is designed to shut down/disconnect and cannot be manually overridden, (2) manufacturer-warranted to shut down on loss of utility service, and (3) properly installed/inspected/tested by utility personnel (Rule 3.01.B); otherwise a visible, lockable, accessible manual disconnect switch is required.
AR.insurance_required: No specific liability insurance dollar minimum found in the rules; only general mutual indemnification language (Appendix A Sec. 8)
AR.ic_timeline_days: Standard Interconnection Agreement review: 30 calendar days (Rule 3.01.E). Preliminary Site Review: 30 days (up to 90 days if multiple concurrent reviews). Facilities Study: utility to use "reasonable efforts" to complete within 120 days (Rule 3.04.G).
AR.non_export_option: No defined non-export/limited-export interconnection pathway found in the rules reviewed -- this is a documented gap, not a confirmed absence at the utility-tariff level
AR.storage_counts_toward_cap: Not explicitly addressed in the rules reviewed
AR.standby_charge: Grid charge authorized only for Legacy customers whose facility exceeds 1,000 kW (up to 20 MW) with Commission approval to exceed the statutory limit; initial rate set to $0.00 effective 6/1/2020 (Rule 2.04.A.3.b-c), utility may later petition to revise upward with a cost-of-service showing

LA.rule_citation: LPSC General Order dated 09-19-2019 (Docket R-33929, Distributed Generation/Net Metering Rules); La. R.S. 45:1177 et seq.
LA.applies_to: IOU + muni + co-op (statute requires investor-owned utilities, municipal utilities, and electric cooperatives to offer net metering; NOTE -- Louisiana has NOT adopted statewide interconnection procedures/technical standards per IREC/Vote Solar's Freeing the Grid project, so interconnection process, timelines, fees, and storage/export provisions are set utility-by-utility, not by a single LPSC rule)
LA.nem_successor: Customers submitting a completed interconnection request and completing installation after 12/31/2019 pay full retail rate for all energy purchased, a zero rate for self-generated/self-consumed energy, and are credited at Avoided Cost for energy exported to the grid (LPSC General Order 9-19-2019). Customers who completed interconnection by 12/31/2019 are grandfathered onto full-retail 1:1 net metering for 15 years (through approximately 2034).
LA.nem_aggregate_cap: 0.5% aggregate cap on solar net-metering participation was removed by the September 2019 rulemaking (Docket R-33929); no aggregate cap currently in force
LA.nem_sizing_rule: Not independently confirmed in this pass (LPSC order text not fully reviewed -- see gaps file)
LA.export_credit_basis: 1:1 retail (legacy, pre-2020 grandfathered only); avoided cost (new, post-2019)
LA.export_credit_value: Avoided Cost is published annually and varies by utility -- LPSC posts a "Avoided Cost Rate by Electric Utility" document each year (2023-2026 editions found at lpsc.louisiana.gov/Utilities_NetMetering); exact cents/kWh figures per utility not extracted in this pass, see source_url
LA.credit_rollover: Not independently confirmed in this pass
LA.annual_true_up: Not independently confirmed in this pass
LA.ic_standard: Not independently confirmed -- no statewide interconnection standard document found; utilities reference their own "Safety and Interconnection Standard" (e.g., Entergy Louisiana)
LA.ic_fast_track_kw: Not independently confirmed (no statewide fast-track tier found)
LA.ic_application_fee: Not independently confirmed -- likely utility-specific tariff fee
LA.external_disconnect: Not independently confirmed -- utility discretion likely given absence of statewide interconnection rule
LA.insurance_required: Not independently confirmed in this pass
LA.ic_timeline_days: Not independently confirmed in this pass
LA.non_export_option: Not independently confirmed -- absence of a statewide interconnection standard means non-export/limited-export pathways, if any, are utility-specific (see utility delta rows for Entergy Louisiana, Cleco, etc. where available)

MS.rule_citation: Mississippi Distributed Generator Interconnection and Net Metering Rules (MPSC Docket, as revised); Miss. Code Ann. 77-3-49
MS.applies_to: IOU only (mandate applies to investor-owned utilities incl. Entergy Mississippi and Mississippi Power; TVA-served areas and munis/co-ops largely outside MPSC net metering jurisdiction -- see Coast Electric Power Association delta row noting ~57% of MS ratepayers, co-op/muni customers, are not bound by this rule)
MS.nem_successor: Not a NEM-to-net-billing transition in the ComEd/AR sense -- MS never had 1:1 retail NEM; export has always been credited at avoided cost plus a Commission-approved "Total Benefits of Distributed Generation" (Value of DG) adder. The adder itself was revised by MPSC order effective ~January 2025 / carried into the 2026 Entergy Mississippi Rate Schedule NEM-2: base adder raised to 5.5 cents/kWh (previously 2.5 cents/kWh in the base rule), with a 7.5 cents/kWh rate for low-to-moderate-income-eligible customers (an increase from the original 2 cents/kWh Low-Income Benefits Adder for the first 1,000 qualifying customers, 15-year guarantee).
MS.nem_aggregate_cap: 3% of the utility's total system peak demand (kW) recorded during the prior calendar year, on a first-come-first-served basis (Ch. 03 Sec. 102-103); current subscription level vs. cap not independently confirmed for Entergy Mississippi or Mississippi Power in this pass
MS.nem_sizing_rule: No sizing-vs-consumption rule; caps are pure nameplate DC capacity limits (20 kW residential / 2 MW non-residential) plus circuit-level screens (e.g., 15% of Line Section peak load)
MS.export_credit_value: Entergy Mississippi NEM-2 (2026): 5.5 cents/kWh excess-credit rate for standard customers; 7.5 cents/kWh for low-to-moderate-income-adder-eligible customers, per Jan. 2025 MPSC order updating the base rule's 2.5 cents/kWh adder
MS.credit_rollover: Indefinite monthly rollover ("each new Billing Period shall begin with zero kWh credits... customer may carry over any value of energy credit arising from the prior Billing Period(s)"); no annual expiry
MS.annual_true_up: No annual true-up month specified in the base rule; credit balance is cashed out only at account closure/termination, net of amounts owed to the utility (Ch. 03 Sec. 105/108)
MS.ic_standard: IEEE 1547 (no specific edition/year cited in rule text -- "as amended and supplemented" language used; IEEE 1547.1 test procedures and IEEE 1547.2 application guide also referenced non-bindingly); UL 1741 similarly referenced without a fixed edition
MS.ic_application_fee: Level 1 (<=20kW, certified inverter-based): no fee unless resubmitted at another level. Level 2 (<=2MW): up to $50 + $1.00/kW, plus engineering costs capped at $100/hr. Level 3 (full study): up to $100 + $2.00/kW, plus actual study/impact costs, engineering capped at $100/hr.
MS.ic_study_trigger_kw: Level 3 full-study review triggers above the Level 2 screens (up to 2 MW, aggregate circuit capacity <2MW) -- exact fail-screen kW threshold not independently isolated from the Level structure in this pass
MS.external_disconnect: Required for Level 2/3 (lockable, visible-break isolation device accessible to the utility); explicitly waived for Level 1 ("Level 1 interconnections do not require an external isolation device")
MS.insurance_required: Not required as a precondition for interconnection approval per the rule and standard application form; utilities barred from requiring insurance not specifically authorized by the rule
MS.ic_timeline_days: Level 1: ~35 business days pre-commissioning (10-day completeness + 15-day approval + witness test within 10 business days of commissioning). Level 2: ~35 business days (10+20+5) plus 30 days for customer signature. Level 3: open-ended, study-duration-dependent (10-day completeness + 10-day scoping + sequential Feasibility/System Impact/Facilities studies with 5-business-day agreement issuance after each), plus 30 business days for customer signature.
MS.non_export_option: Not addressed -- the rule contains no mention of "storage" or "battery" anywhere in the text; energy storage interconnection, grid-charging, and non-export/limited-export pathways are undefined gaps in Mississippi's DG rule
MS.storage_counts_toward_cap: Not addressed (rule silent on storage generally)
MS.standby_charge: Prohibited -- Ch. 03 Sec. 111: EU shall not charge any back-up, standby, or Exit Fees to a net-metering customer unless otherwise approved by the Commission
MS.standby_threshold_kw: Not applicable given the standby-charge prohibition

TX.jurisdiction_body: Public Utility Commission of Texas (PUCT) -- applies only to the small non-ERCOT, MISO-served portion of the state (Entergy Texas territory); ERCOT-area distribution utilities/co-ops/munis are NOT subject to these PUCT DG/net-metering rules
TX.rule_citation: 16 TAC 25.211 (Interconnection of On-Site Distributed Generation); 16 TAC 25.212 (Technical Requirements); 16 TAC 25.242 (limited net metering for non-unbundled/integrated IOUs)
TX.applies_to: IOU only -- and critically, only the small slice of Texas still served by a vertically-integrated, non-unbundled IOU (Entergy Texas Inc., which is in MISO, not ERCOT). CRITICAL DISTINCTION: over 75% of Texas load is in ERCOT under retail choice, where PUCT has NOT adopted net-metering rules -- solar/storage export compensation there is entirely a matter of private contract with a competitive Retail Electric Provider ("solar buyback plan"), not a regulatory mandate. Munis and co-ops statewide (in both ERCOT and MISO footprints) are exempt from PUCT jurisdiction entirely.
TX.nem_successor: No statewide net-metering successor -- Texas has never had a statewide 1:1 NEM mandate. In the Entergy Texas/MISO territory, PUCT's limited net-metering rule (16 TAC 25.242) requires integrated IOUs to offer net metering to qualifying facilities, but export is credited at avoided cost, not retail. In ERCOT territory, there is no rule at all -- export compensation exists only via voluntary competitive-market "solar buyback" retail plans.
TX.nem_aggregate_cap: Not a percentage-of-peak-load aggregate cap under 16 TAC 25.242; program availability is bounded only by the per-customer size ceilings (50 kW renewable / 100 kW non-renewable) and standard first-come interconnection processing
TX.nem_sizing_rule: Not independently confirmed in this pass
TX.export_credit_basis: avoided cost (Entergy Texas/MISO territory only via Schedule SQF); not applicable statewide / contract-based in ERCOT
TX.export_credit_value: Entergy Texas Schedule SQF: avoided cost calculated as an average of peak and off-peak rates per the utility's latest annual PUCT filing; no single statewide cents/kWh figure exists given the ERCOT/MISO split and competitive-market pricing in ERCOT
TX.credit_rollover: Not independently confirmed for Entergy Texas Schedule SQF in this pass
TX.annual_true_up: Not independently confirmed in this pass
TX.ic_standard: IEEE 1547-2018 baseline cited in PUCT interconnection application guidance (UL 1741 certification also required for inverters); exact rule-text edition citation and any transition timeline not independently confirmed in this pass
TX.ic_fast_track_kw: Not independently confirmed with a specific fast-track kW threshold in 16 TAC 25.211
TX.ic_study_trigger_kw: 10000 (16 TAC 25.211 covers IOU interconnections of generators up to 10 MW; screens for review tiers within that ceiling not independently confirmed in this pass)
TX.external_disconnect: Not independently confirmed in this pass
TX.insurance_required: Not independently confirmed in this pass
TX.ic_timeline_days: Not independently confirmed in this pass
TX.non_export_option: Not independently confirmed for Entergy Texas/PUCT rules in this pass; in ERCOT territory any non-export configuration would be a competitive-market/REP contract matter, not a PUCT rule

PA.rule_citation: 52 Pa. Code Ch. 75 (Subchapter B Net Metering, Subchapter C Interconnection); AEPS Act 213 of 2004 as amended by Act 129 of 2008, 73 P.S. Section 1648.2 (customer-generator definition)
PA.applies_to: IOU only (Chapter 75 binds PUC-jurisdictional EDCs; municipal and rural electric cooperatives are exempt and set own rules)
PA.nem_aggregate_cap: No statewide aggregate cap identified in Chapter 75 or AEPS Act (unlike NJ/MD/DE)
PA.nem_sizing_rule: <=200% of customer-generator's expected/historical annual electricity consumption (AEPS Act 213 statutory definition of 'customer-generator', 73 P.S. Section 1648.2; raised from 110% to 200% by amendment). Note: PUC's 2016 rulemaking had proposed re-codifying a 200% sizing cap directly into 52 Pa. Code Section 75.13, but IRRC found the Commission lacked authority to add it in regulation and it was struck from the final-form rule -- the 200% limit therefore rests on the statutory customer-generator definition, not the regulation text.
PA.annual_true_up: Annual true-up at EDC's Price-to-Compare (PTC) rate -- default-service generation+transmission supply rate, excludes distribution charges; timing varies by EDC (e.g., West Penn May 31)
PA.ic_standard: IEEE 1547 + UL 1741 (utilities such as PPL now require UL 1741 Supplement B / IEEE 1547-2018 compliance; no single statewide mandatory transition date found in Chapter 75 text itself)
PA.ic_application_fee: Level 1 (<=10kW): $100 flat. Level 2 (>10kW-2MW): $250 + $1/kW + cost of minor modifications. Level 3 (>2MW or non-conforming): $350 + $2/kW + cost of feasibility/system impact/facilities studies.
PA.external_disconnect: Required (accessible external disconnect switch or utility access to one)
PA.insurance_required: Unclear -- not confirmed in sources reviewed
PA.ic_timeline_days: Unclear -- statutory review timelines exist in Ch. 75 Subchapter C but exact day-counts not independently verified this pass
PA.grid_charging_allowed: Unclear -- Chapter 75 does not explicitly address grid-charging of storage independent of net metering; EDC interpretations reportedly differ and have produced PUC disputes
PA.non_export_option: Unclear -- no explicit non-export/limited-export interconnection pathway identified in Chapter 75 text reviewed; likely handled case-by-case under Level 3/facilities study process
PA.storage_counts_toward_cap: Unclear -- not confirmed whether battery nameplate kW counts toward the 50kW/3MW system cap or only the inverter's AC export rating

NJ.jurisdiction_body: New Jersey Board of Public Utilities
NJ.rule_citation: N.J.S.A. 48:3-87; N.J.A.C. 14:8-4 (Net Metering) and 14:8-5 (Interconnection); Clean Energy Act of 2018 (P.L.2018 c.17)
NJ.applies_to: IOU only (municipal electric utilities and rural electric cooperatives -- there are very few in NJ -- generally exempt from BPU jurisdiction)
NJ.nem_cap_res_kw: 10 (Level 1 residential; Level 1 nonresidential threshold differs, see nonres cap cell)
NJ.nem_aggregate_cap: 5.8% of total annual kWh sold statewide by each electric power supplier in the prior year (N.J.S.A. 48:3-87). This is a discretionary trigger, not an automatic cutoff -- BPU may authorize suppliers to stop offering NEM to new customers once reached, but may also continue past it. BPU held stakeholder workshops in late 2024 ('Jurisdictional Survey of NEM Reforms') on potential reform; docket ongoing as of 2026 -- watch for a live rulemaking that could change this cell.
NJ.nem_sizing_rule: No statewide sizing-to-load limit identified beyond the Level 1/2/3 capacity tiers themselves (10kW Level 1 residential / 25kW Level 1 nonresidential / 2000kW Level 2 / Level 3 above that)
NJ.annual_true_up: Annual true-up: excess NEG at year-end trued up at supplier avoided-cost/wholesale rate (not retail)
NJ.ic_application_fee: Level 1: no fee. Level 2: $50 + $1/kW. Level 3: $100 + $2/kW (per pre-2024 rule; a Chapter 8 'Grid Modernization' rulemaking proposed updates to these fees and thresholds in 2024 -- confirm current fee schedule before quoting).
NJ.external_disconnect: Required per N.J.A.C. 14:8-5 general interconnection provisions
NJ.insurance_required: Unclear -- not independently confirmed this pass
NJ.ic_timeline_days: Unclear -- Level 3 review timelines were subject to 2024 proposed amendments (N.J.A.C. 14:8-5.6); exact day-counts not verified
NJ.grid_charging_allowed: Yes-with-conditions -- BPU is actively expanding storage participation (Garden State Energy Storage Program, 1,000 MW transmission-scale target across Tranches 1-2 as of March 2026; SREC-II/CSI Tranche 5 storage adders for net-metered solar >5MW). No blanket prohibition on grid-charging identified, but incentive program eligibility and crediting treatment vary by program track (SuSI/SREC-II vs. GSESP) -- verify per-project before assuming arbitrage revenue stacks with incentives.
NJ.non_export_option: Yes -- N.J.A.C. defines 'non-exporting' customer-generator facilities and permits electric devices designed to limit/prevent injection to the grid, used to bypass full net-metering/interconnection study requirements.
NJ.storage_counts_toward_cap: Unclear -- not confirmed whether battery-only nameplate capacity counts toward Level 1/2/3 thresholds or only combined system export rating

DE.rule_citation: 26 Del. C. Section 1014 (Net Energy Metering); Delmarva/DEC/DEMEC file own implementing rules per statute
DE.applies_to: IOU + co-op + muni (statute directs PSC, municipal electric companies, AND electric cooperatives to EACH promulgate their own net-metering rules -- Delaware Electric Cooperative and the DEMEC municipal members are NOT bound by PSC-adopted rules and can and do set their own terms; see utility file for DEC/DEMEC deltas)
DE.nem_cap_nonres_kw: 2000 (Delmarva) / 500 (DEC or a DEMEC municipal electric company)
DE.nem_aggregate_cap: 8% of the capacity necessary to meet the electric utility's average Delaware transmission peak demand over the preceding 3 years, calculated in MW-AC (26 Del. C. Section 1014, as amended by SB 298 in 2022, which raised the cap from 5% to 8%); utility may elect to stop offering NEM to new customer-generators once exceeded -- current statewide subscription level not found this pass, but cap was raised specifically to buy '2-3 years for net-metering 2.0 discussions' per DEMEC's 2022 board presentation, implying it was approaching the prior 5% cap -- treat as a live/moderate risk area to re-check.
DE.nem_sizing_rule: No statutory sizing-to-load percentage limit found (cap is a flat kW limit per customer/meter class); however customers are only credited up to 100% of their own annual usage -- oversized systems do not earn a payout for the excess (SB 298, 2022), effectively discouraging intentional oversizing even though there's no hard kW-vs-load design cap.
DE.credit_rollover: Annual expiry, CONFIRMED -- SB 298 (2022) amended 26 Del. C. Section 1014 so that at the end of the annualized billing period, excess (net) kWh credits REVERT TO THE UTILITY with no monetary payout and no rollover into the next annual period (this ended the prior practice of annual cash-out at avoided cost). Applies to DEC/DEMEC per DEMEC's 2022 policy briefing; Delmarva DE's practice not independently confirmed but the statutory change should apply utility-wide since it amended the underlying Title 26 statute -- verify Delmarva's specific tariff language.
DE.annual_true_up: Customer selects annualized billing/true-up period (recommended practice per DEMEC is a period ending in March/April, since credits build in summer and are best used through winter; DE Electric Coop initially set Dec year-end amid customer backlash, then moved to a period ending in March). Non-residential customers pay full cost of any new/replacement net meter; residential customers pay up to $200 (SB 298).
DE.ic_standard: National Electrical Code + IEEE + UL standards for systems <=25kW (statutory reference to NEC/IEEE/UL compliance rather than a named interconnection standard doc); IEEE 1547 version/UL 1741 supplement not specified in sources reviewed
DE.ic_application_fee: Not independently confirmed this pass -- Delmarva publishes its own interconnection guidelines
DE.grid_charging_allowed: Unclear -- no DE-specific grid-charging provision identified in the statute; likely governed by each utility's own interconnection tariff (see Delmarva DE / DEC / DEMEC utility rows)
DE.non_export_option: Unclear -- not confirmed whether DE has a defined non-export interconnection pathway distinct from the standard NEM/interconnection process

MD.rule_citation: COMAR 20.50.10 (Net Metering); COMAR 20.50.09 (Small Generator Interconnection Standards); Md. PUA Section 7-306
MD.applies_to: IOU + co-op (net metering/interconnection duties run to 'electric companies' which under PUA include cooperatives; municipal utilities such as Easton, Berlin, Hagerstown, Thurmont, Williamsport participate voluntarily and are shown reporting net-metering data in PSC reports, so treat as All utilities for MD net metering specifically)
MD.nem_cap_res_kw: No separate residential-only cap identified -- 2 MW applies per customer-generator regardless of class (see nem_cap_nonres_kw)
MD.nem_aggregate_cap: 3,000 MW statewide aggregate cap (PUA Section 7-306(g), doubled from 1,500 MW effective 10/1/2021; ~18.45% of MD peak demand). As of PSC's Nov 2025 report: installed capacity ~1,537 MW = 51.23% of cap, BUT the pending Community Solar pipeline (~2,911 MW: 700 MW awaiting authorization + 1,728 MW in interconnection queues + 483 MW accepted-not-operating) will nearly exhaust the cap on its own -- PSC's central 2025 recommendation is that the General Assembly act in the 2026 session to raise or restructure the cap. THIS IS A LIVE, HIGH-RISK DOCKET for MD deal screening.
MD.nem_sizing_rule: <=200% of the customer-generator's annual baseline kWh use (COMAR 20.50.10)
MD.credit_rollover: Customer may elect (since SB143, eff. 10/1/2023) to accrue net excess generation (NEG) indefinitely rather than annual cash-out; if annual payout is elected, paid within 30 days after the billing cycle closest to end of April at the generation/commodity portion of the rate averaged over the prior 12 months
MD.ic_application_fee: Level 1 (<=20kW): no fee. Level 2 (<=2MW): $50 + $1/kW. Level 3/4 (network circuits / non-exporting / studies required): $100 + $2/kW.
MD.external_disconnect: Not independently confirmed this pass (COMAR 20.50.09 text not fully retrieved)
MD.grid_charging_allowed: Yes-with-conditions -- MD PSC has approved DRIVE Act EDSSS (Electric Distribution System Support Services) pilots at BGE, Pepco, and Potomac Edison (~185.7 MW combined target) compensating customer-sited batteries and bidirectional EVs for grid services, e.g. up to $300/kW-yr for a 10kW bidirectional resource. NOTE: brief's characterization as a 'BYOD storage tariff' program was not confirmed verbatim in sources reviewed -- the mechanism found is the DRIVE Act EDSSS pilot (Order following 7/1/2025 Commission directive), not a program literally named 'Bring Your Own Device.' Underlying substance (customer-owned storage dispatched for utility/grid value, separate from net metering) matches the brief's intent; SMECO was not identified among the filing utilities (BGE, Pepco, Delmarva, Potomac Edison only) -- flagged for verification.
MD.non_export_option: Level 3 (COMAR 20.50.09) explicitly covers interconnection requests to area networks/radial circuits 'when electric power is not exported to the electric distribution system' -- i.e., MD has an explicit non-export interconnection review track.
MD.storage_counts_toward_cap: Yes -- MD's 2 MW cap and 200%-of-baseline sizing rule apply to 'electric generating system' capacity, which for solar+storage projects is generally read to include the paired storage nameplate for purposes of the net-metering system size cap (not independently confirmed against COMAR text for storage-specific treatment -- verify)

DC.jurisdiction_body: Public Service Commission of the District of Columbia (net metering/interconnection); DC Department of Energy & Environment / DOEE (SREC/RPS program)
DC.rule_citation: 15 DCMR Chapter 9 (Net Energy Metering Rules) and Chapter 40 (Small Generator Interconnection Rules -- SGIR)
DC.applies_to: IOU only (Pepco is the sole electric distribution company serving the District, so this is effectively a single-utility jurisdiction)
DC.nem_aggregate_cap: No aggregate capacity limit identified for DC net metering (unlike PA/NJ/MD/DE)
DC.nem_sizing_rule: Sizing limit was phased in: capped at 140% of customer's historical 12-month usage effective 1/1/2021, increasing 20 percentage points/year until reaching <=200% of historical 12-month usage by 2024 and thereafter
DC.export_credit_value: ~$0.13-0.15/kWh effective retail-rate equivalent (varies by rate class; not a separately published per-kWh export rate since compensation is via retail bill credit)
DC.annual_true_up: December: any remaining NEG (net excess generation) at that point is compensated in cash at the generation rate only (not full retail) -- confirmed via Pepco DC net metering tariff summary; systems <=100kW
DC.ic_standard: IEEE 1547 (+ UL 1741 / IEEE 1547.1 for lab-certified equipment)
DC.external_disconnect: Waived for systems <10kW; required for all other systems (>=10kW)
DC.grid_charging_allowed: Unclear -- no DC-specific grid-charging provision for storage identified in 15 DCMR Ch. 9/40 text reviewed
DC.non_export_option: Unclear -- not confirmed whether DC's SGIR (Ch. 40) defines a distinct non-export/limited-export interconnection pathway

VA.rule_citation: Va. Code § 56-594 (IOU net metering); § 56-594.01 (electric cooperative net metering); 20VAC5-315 (Net Energy Metering regs); 20VAC5-314 (Interconnection of Small Electrical Generators)
VA.applies_to: IOU + co-op + muni, but co-ops operate under separate § 56-594.01 program with their own caps, and municipal utilities (e.g. Danville, Harrisonburg, Manassas) are not subject to SCC jurisdiction and set their own net metering policy by local ordinance/utility commission action
VA.nem_successor: Not closed; Dominion Energy Virginia customers interconnecting after the SCC's April 30, 2026 final order in Case No. PUR-2025-00079 move to a new 'NEM 2.0' tariff that keeps 1:1 kWh crediting and 12-month (annual) netting, but changes the year-end net-excess-generation cash-out rate to $0.05829/kWh (previously avoided cost, ~3.5c/kWh) and adds a $1/month admin fee; all pre-order Dominion NEM customers are grandfathered indefinitely on legacy terms. APCo's parallel NEM case was decided in the utility's favor (no material changes) in Sept. 2025. Dominion required to file revised tariffs within 90 days of the 4/30/2026 order (~by 7/29/2026).
VA.nem_cap_res_kw: 25 kW AC (IOU default under § 56-594; co-op default is 20 kW AC per § 56-594.01 program, varies slightly by co-op rider)
VA.nem_cap_nonres_kw: 3 MW (statutory cap under § 56-594 for nonresidential eligible customer-generators; individual IOU tariffs may set lower nonresidential program sub-caps, e.g. Dominion caps at 1 MW)
VA.nem_aggregate_cap: 6% of each utility's prior-year peak load (raised from 1% by the 2020 Virginia Clean Economy Act), with 1 percentage point of the 6% reserved for low-income program participants; as of 2026 SCC filings, Dominion and APCo both report participation well under the 6% cap statewide, though specific co-op sub-caps are much closer to full in some territories (see utility file for local subscription levels)
VA.nem_sizing_rule: System generating capacity may not exceed expected annual energy consumption based on the customer's own usage history (no fixed % sizing rule; utility discretion to verify via 12-month billing history)
VA.export_credit_value: 1:1 retail credit throughout the year for both IOUs and co-ops; Dominion year-end net-excess-generation cash-out is $0.05829/kWh effective for NEM 2.0 customers per the April 30, 2026 SCC order (legacy Dominion customers retain avoided-cost cash-out, historically ~3.5c/kWh); APCo year-end excess purchased at avoided cost (~3.5c/kWh, 2019 figure, last published)
VA.credit_rollover: indefinite monthly rollover within the annual period
VA.annual_true_up: Annual true-up date varies by utility (typically customer's April/anniversary billing cycle); excess above what's used in the true-up period is cashed out at avoided cost (APCo, legacy Dominion) or $0.05829/kWh (Dominion NEM 2.0, new interconnections)
VA.ic_fast_track_kw: Not explicitly tiered as 'fast track' in 20VAC5-314; Level 1 process covers inverter-based systems meeting UL 1741-SB certification requirements
VA.ic_simplified_kw: Level 1 threshold effectively covers most residential/small C&I systems (see ic_application_fee tiers); Level 2/3 required for larger or non-certified systems
VA.ic_application_fee: $100 (Level 1 processing fee); $1,000 (Levels 2 and 3 processing fee); $500 nonrefundable fee for a pre-application report; up to $50 inverter-settings inspection fee
VA.ic_study_trigger_kw: Level 2/3 review triggers for systems not qualifying for Level 1 (generally above small inverter-certified systems; SGF regulation covers systems up to 500 kW)
VA.external_disconnect: Utility discretion (readily accessible, lockable, visible disconnect commonly required by utility interconnection agreements; not uniformly mandated in statute for all inverter-based systems)
VA.insurance_required: Yes — liability insurance required, historically $100,000 for systems <=10 kW and $300,000 for systems >10-20 kW (co-op figures; IOU requirements similar order of magnitude, confirm per utility)
VA.ic_timeline_days: Not codified as a fixed statewide day-count in the reviewed sources; utilities target order-of-weeks for Level 1 inverter-certified systems
VA.non_export_option: Yes — non-export/limited-export interconnection paths exist for larger systems seeking to avoid full interconnection studies, per utility TIIR/interconnection procedures (utility-specific; not detailed in state-level source reviewed)
VA.storage_counts_toward_cap: Unclear (not explicitly addressed in state-level sources reviewed; utility practice may vary — see utility file and storage_specific_notes)
VA.standby_charge: Yes — SCC-authorized standby charge for net-metered residential customers of Dominion Energy Virginia above the AC capacity threshold
VA.standby_threshold_kw: 20 kW AC effective July 1, 2026 under HB 1255 (raised from 15 kW AC, which itself succeeded the original 10 kW AC threshold set in 2011 under HB 1983); threshold applies to aggregate nameplate AC capacity of the customer's generating facility as stated on interconnection paperwork, not actual production

WV.rule_citation: W. Va. Code § 24-2F-8 (net metering and interconnection standards); 150 CSR 33 (Rules Governing Electric Utility Net Metering Arrangements and Interconnections)
WV.applies_to: All utilities offering net metering (IOU, municipal utilities serving >=30,000 customers, and rural electric cooperatives are all contemplated by statute; the PSC 'shall consider adopting' a rule extending net metering to smaller munis/co-ops, so smaller munis/co-ops may not be obligated to offer it — confirm per utility)
WV.nem_successor: Net billing (fixed volumetric export rate) has replaced 1:1 retail crediting for NEW net metering customers of Appalachian Power Co. and Wheeling Power Co. following the PSC's August 2025 rate case order; new AEP-WV enrollees after an extended grandfathering window (application submitted after 2/28/2026) receive a fixed export credit of approximately 12.4 cents/kWh (67-75% of full retail rate) instead of 1:1. Separately, Monongahela Power and Potomac Edison (FirstEnergy) customers who interconnect on/after 1/1/2025 receive fixed rates of 9.34c/kWh (residential/schools/churches/general service), 9.15c/kWh (large general service), or 8.91c/kWh (large power/alternative generation) per the 2024 PSC-approved settlement (effective 3/27/2024); existing (legacy/grandfathered) customers of all four IOUs remain on 1:1 full retail net metering, with Mon Power/Potomac Edison legacy customers explicitly grandfathered for 25 years from the settlement date.
WV.nem_cap_res_kw: 25 kW AC (statewide statutory/PSC-rule cap for residential, per W. Va. Code § 24-2F-8 and Level 1 interconnection definition in 150 CSR 33 / AEP TIIR)
WV.nem_cap_nonres_kw: 500 kW (commercial cap per current AEP/FirstEnergy tariffs, consistent with § 24-2F-8(f) directive that PSC consider raising commercial cap to 500 kW); 2 MW (industrial cap per current AEP/FirstEnergy tariffs, consistent with § 24-2F-8(f) directive re: industrial cap up to 2 MW)
WV.nem_aggregate_cap: 3% of each electric utility's aggregate customer peak demand in West Virginia during the previous year, with no less than 0.5% of that reserved specifically for residential customer-generators (W. Va. Code § 24-2F-8(g)); current subscription level as a % of the cap not published in sources reviewed
WV.nem_sizing_rule: No fixed statewide sizing percentage found in statute or PSC rule reviewed; utility interconnection agreements govern via nameplate AC capacity caps rather than a load-based sizing formula
WV.export_credit_basis: Mixed — 1:1 retail (legacy/grandfathered customers, all four IOUs) or fixed volumetric export rate (new customers post-reform)
WV.export_credit_value: Legacy/grandfathered: 1:1 retail. New AEP-WV (Appalachian Power, Wheeling Power) customers after grandfathering window closes: ~12.4 cents/kWh (PSC order, Aug. 2025). New Mon Power/Potomac Edison customers on/after 1/1/2025: 9.34c/kWh (residential/schools/churches/general service), 9.15c/kWh (large general service), 8.91c/kWh (large power/alternative generation) — rates fixed for 2025-2026 per 2024 settlement, subject to renegotiation in the companies' 2026 ENEC case.
WV.credit_rollover: Indefinite for legacy 1:1 customers (grandfathered 25 years from interconnection/settlement date for Mon Power/Potomac Edison); monthly/annual treatment for new fixed-rate customers not fully detailed in sources reviewed
WV.annual_true_up: Excess credited against the energy portion of the bill only (not fixed/demand charges) for Mon Power/Potomac Edison per 2024 settlement; AEP-WV true-up treatment for new fixed-rate customers not fully detailed in sources reviewed
WV.ic_standard: IEEE 1547 (with IEEE 1547.1 testing protocols) + UL 1741-SB (per AEP WV Net Metering Customer Information Guide v2.0, eff. 2/1/2026)
WV.ic_fast_track_kw: Level 1: nameplate capacity <=25 kW, inverter-based, non-islanding, UL-listed/certified per Appendix C of 150 CSR 33, interconnecting at <=69kV
WV.ic_simplified_kw: Level 1 threshold effectively serves as the simplified/fast-track tier (<=25 kW)
WV.ic_application_fee: $30 (Level 1); $50 + $1/kW of capacity (Level 2, i.e. any system not qualifying for Level 1)
WV.ic_study_trigger_kw: Level 2 interconnection required for any system not meeting Level 1 criteria (effectively >25 kW or non-conforming equipment)
WV.external_disconnect: Required — labeled, lockable, visible load-break disconnect required outside near the utility meter (per AEP WV TIIR)
WV.insurance_required: Yes — minimum $100,000 general liability insurance required while interconnected
WV.ic_timeline_days: Not codified as a fixed statutory day-count in sources reviewed; AEP process includes 10-business-day review windows at multiple steps (test results, submittal review, meter installation)
WV.non_export_option: Unclear — not detailed in state-level statute or PSC rule sources reviewed; utility TIIR documents may define non-export paths for larger systems (see utility file)
WV.storage_counts_toward_cap: Unclear (not addressed in state-level sources reviewed)
WV.standby_charge: No statewide standby charge identified in W. Va. Code § 24-2F-8 or 150 CSR 33 as reviewed; utilities have not been found to assess a distinct 'standby charge' analogous to Virginia's — the 2025 AEP-WV net-metering reform instead restructured the ongoing export credit rate itself rather than adding a separate demand-based standby fee
